events.text:
## Recommendation
- Pier fishing is a guess this week. No report in the last 4 weeks covers a pier at these ports, so I can't rate it from DNR data.
- My estimate: St. Joseph about 2/4, South Haven about 2/4, Grand Haven about 1/4, Muskegon about 1/4. Go to St. Joseph first.
- Start with spoons or meat rigs near the pier. That's what boat anglers used (South Haven, 2023-07-05; Grand Haven, 2023-06-21), so treat it as a starting point, not a pier-specific finding.
- Check the wind before you go. I don't have a live forecast, so look at the forecast yourself.

## Why
- I'd expect St. Joseph to be the best pier bet because its nearshore satellite water is the warmest of the four (72 F) and it had the most recent upwelling-favorable wind, which can bring fish to the pier.
- The latest boat report at St. Joseph was average, while Grand Haven's and Muskegon's were slow or only fair, so I'd expect the same ranking for piers.
- I'd expect Grand Haven and Muskegon to be weaker because their nearshore water warmed and had little upwelling wind in the last 3 days before today.

## Evidence
**Recent reports (last 4 weeks)**
- The newest report is St. Joseph and South Haven, 2023-07-05 (13 days old). Both were boat-only: South Haven was "fair" (quality 1) with fish about 100 ft down on spoons, and St. Joseph was "decent" (quality 2) in 120+ ft of water.
- Grand Haven's newest is 2023-06-21 (27 days old), boat only, quality 2 (fish 35-90 ft down, orange spoons and meat rigs).
- Muskegon has no report in this window; its newest is 41 days old.
- No report in this window mentions a pier at any of the four ports.

**Past seasons (similar water temperature, about 70 F, mid-July ±3 weeks)**
- These are also boat reports, not pier reports. Most were slow to fair (quality 0-1). The one average was St. Joseph, 2022-06-29 (quality 2), on rotators and flies.
- Grand Haven and Muskegon, 2022-07-14: slow (quality 0). South Haven and St. Joseph, 2022-07-06: slow to spotty.
- I'd expect this pattern to repeat: slow to fair fishing in this temperature range.

**Conditions (summary for the week before today, not a live forecast)**
- St. Joseph: nearshore satellite water 72 F, up 1 F in the last 3 days. Upwelling wind 10 hours in 7 days, 4 hours in the last 3 days. Buoy 71 F.
- South Haven: nearshore satellite water 72 F, up 1 F in the last 3 days. Upwelling wind 4 hours in 7 days, none in the last 3 days. Buoy 71 F.
- Grand Haven: nearshore satellite water 70 F, up 2 F in the last 3 days. Upwelling wind 11 hours in 7 days, none in the last 3 days. Buoy 68 F.
- Muskegon: nearshore satellite water 69 F, up 2 F in the last 3 days. Upwelling wind 11 hours in 7 days, 1 hour in the last 3 days. Buoy 68 F.
- Upwelling would cool the nearshore water; the warming and calm recent wind suggest it hasn't happened lately at these ports.

## Caveats
- The newest report is 13 days old (St. Joseph and South Haven) and the others are older. Treat all of this as a guide.
- The 0-4 pier ratings are my estimates from boat reports and water conditions. They are not DNR pier ratings.
- The water data is satellite (near the pier) and buoy (offshore), not a measured reading at the pier. The satellite values can lag 1-2 days.
- The conditions tool returned a summary for the week before today, not a live forecast. Check this weekend's wind yourself.

## Sources
- South Haven and St. Joseph, 2023-07-05: https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/MIDNR/bulletins/363ad03
- Grand Haven, South Haven and St. Joseph, 2023-06-21: https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/MIDNR/bulletins/3614332
